title: X11: Windows can remain missing from the Task Manager after WM_TRANSIENT_FOR is removed
line: The reporter's open MR !7387 makes the Task Manager highlight the focused window's task after that window stops being a transient (Java dialogs), verified on the rig.
explanation: On Wayland the task model only works out which task is active when a window's active state changes, by walking up to its transient parent at that moment. When a focused dialog later loses its parent (its owner window is hidden, or the X11 app drops WM_TRANSIENT_FOR) and becomes its own task, nothing recomputes it, so no task is highlighted until you click away and back; the same happens when the parent link arrives after the dialog was activated. MR !7387 remembers the focused window separately and recomputes the active task whenever that window's parent chain changes or a window in it goes away.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: Update active Wayland tasks when transient parents change

Track the active Wayland window separately from the task representing it.
Update the represented active task when its transient parent chain changes,
including when the former parent is unmapped.

CCBUG: 527381

media.caption: Pure master, reporter's AwtTransientRepro --keep-focus with an extra Icons-and-Text Task Manager (grouping off) on top: open the dialog, then Hide FIRST FRAME. No task is highlighted at any point after the dialog opens.
Same steps with MR !7387: FIRST FRAME's task stays active while its dialog is focused, and the ACTIVE DIALOG task is active after FIRST FRAME is hidden.
Master after Hide FIRST FRAME: KWin's active window is ACTIVE DIALOG, but neither task manager highlights its task.
With the MR: the ACTIVE DIALOG task is highlighted in both task managers.
Top task manager on master: FIRST FRAME alone (active), with the transient dialog focused (not active), after hiding FIRST FRAME (dialog task not active).
Same three moments with the MR: the task holding the focused window is highlighted each time.
